tools.name: list_servers
tools.title: List servers
tools.description: List the database servers you may use: logical name, kind (postgres, mongo, redis), description and `databases` — each with the actions, tools and limits your grants give you there. No connection info. Start here.

tools.name: list_databases
tools.title: List databases
tools.description: List the databases you may use on `server`, or on every server you can see when `server` is omitted: logical name, description, kind, your actions, whether writes can succeed, the tools that work there and the row/timeout/reason limits your grants enforce. No connection info.

server.description: Logical server name from list_servers; omit for all.

tools.name: describe_schema
tools.title: Describe schema
tools.description: Tables, columns and types of a database. `detail`: `names` (tables and their kind), `columns` (default), `full` (real types, keys, indexes, comments, row estimates). Optional `schema` (default `public`) and `table` narrow the result; `search` keeps tables whose name or a column name contains the term, across every schema unless `schema` is given. Mongo: collections and their indexes (`schema` ignored); `full` also infers fields from a few sampled documents, which needs query_read. Not on Redis. Needs schema_read.

search.description: Case-insensitive substring of a table or column name.

reason.description: Why you are making this call; required when the grant sets require_reason.

tools.name: sample_table
tools.title: Sample table
tools.description: A few rows of one table — `SELECT * FROM "<schema>"."<table>" LIMIT n`, default 10 rows, at most 100,000; `columns` keeps only those. Mongo: a limited `find` on the collection, one `document` column per row (`columns` picks top-level fields). Not on Redis. Schema and table are plain identifiers (letters, digits, `_`; a Mongo collection may also hold `-` and `.`). Same result shape as run_query. Needs query_read.

max_bytes.description: Cap on the JSON size of the returned rows: the leading rows that fit are kept, truncated_by: byte_cap.

max_cell_bytes.description: Replace any cell whose JSON is longer with a {"$dbmcp_truncated": {bytes, preview}} marker; drops no row.

reason.description: Why you are making this call; required when the grant sets require_reason.

tools.name: explain
tools.title: Explain query
tools.description: The query plan from `EXPLAIN (FORMAT JSON)`, plus a `summary`: the root's total_cost and plan_rows, seq_scans (relations read by a sequential scan) and node_count. Plain EXPLAIN never executes the statement; INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE need a query_write grant. `analyze: true` runs the statement for real timings — read statements only, inside a read-only transaction and the 30 s statement timeout. Postgres only.

params.description: Postgres only: values bound to $1..$n, in order — never parsed as SQL. JSON null, boolean, integer, number, string, array/object bind as an untyped NULL, bool, int8, float8, text, jsonb; cast in the SQL for any other type ($1::date). At most 100, each at most 64 KiB of JSON.

reason.description: Why you are making this call; required when the grant sets require_reason.

tools.name: run_query
tools.title: Run query
tools.description: Run one statement under your grants. `sql` depends on the server kind (see its description). Returns columns, rows, truncated, row_limit, elapsed_ms and, for a write, rows_affected. Rows: default 1,000, `limit` up to 100,000, a grant may lower both; a result stops at 32 MiB. When `truncated`, `truncated_by` says which cap hit and `hint` how to page for the rest. Statement timeout 30 s (a grant may lower it). Read-only unless a query_write grant allows one INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE on Postgres; `dry_run: true` runs that write and rolls it back (triggers fire; sequences advance). Mongo and Redis are always read-only.

sql.description: By server kind: postgres — one SQL statement; mongo — a JSON command document, e.g. {"find":"users","filter":{}}; redis — a JSON argv array, e.g. ["HGETALL","user:1"].

params.description: Postgres only: values bound to $1..$n, in order — never parsed as SQL. JSON null, boolean, integer, number, string, array/object bind as an untyped NULL, bool, int8, float8, text, jsonb; cast in the SQL for any other type ($1::date). At most 100, each at most 64 KiB of JSON.

max_bytes.description: Cap on the JSON size of the returned rows: the leading rows that fit are kept, truncated_by: byte_cap.

max_cell_bytes.description: Replace any cell whose JSON is longer with a {"$dbmcp_truncated": {bytes, preview}} marker; drops no row.

reason.description: Why you are making this call; required when the grant sets require_reason.

tools.name: get_query_history
tools.title: Query history
tools.description: Your recent queries against a (server, database), newest first: SQL and its sql_sha256, timestamp, duration, row count and outcome; `sql_sha256` narrows to one statement's runs. Recovers context across sessions. Scoped to your authenticated identity, never to a client-supplied user; a service token that sends `x-dbmcp-run-id` sees only that run's entries. Needs history_read.

since.description: RFC 3339 timestamp; only entries occurred at or after this instant are returned.

limit.description: Max entries to return; clamped to the gateway ceiling.

cursor.description: Opaque `next_cursor` from a previous page; returns the entries after it.

sql_sha256.description: Hex SHA-256 of the stored SQL (an entry's sql_sha256); only its entries are returned.

reason.description: Why you are making this call; required when the grant sets require_reason.

tools.name: table_stats
tools.title: Table stats
tools.description: Table health for a schema (default `public`) or one table: total size, row estimate, dead tuples, last vacuum/analyze, and per-index size + scan count. Postgres only. Needs schema_read.

reason.description: Why you are making this call; required when the grant sets require_reason.

tools.name: db_activity
tools.title: Database activity
tools.description: Your own statements the gateway is running on this database right now: pid, request_id, pool, state, wait event and running_ms. No query text — see get_query_history. Postgres only. Needs schema_read.

reason.description: Why you are making this call; required when the grant sets require_reason.

run_scoped.description: Service accounts only: true refuses the call (invalid_arguments) unless it carries x-dbmcp-run-id, so it covers that run's statements only. The run id is unverified: a filter, not isolation.

tools.name: cancel_query
tools.title: Cancel query
tools.description: Cancel one of your own running queries by its gateway `request_id` (from the error body, `x-request-id`, or db_activity). Postgres only. Needs query_read on the database.

reason.description: Why you are making this call; required when the grant sets require_reason.

tools.name: whoami
tools.title: Who am I
tools.description: Your authenticated identity, groups, session expiry and the grants that apply to you. No database call.
